name: The four establishments of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhāna)
method_summary: The monk abides contemplating the body in the body, feelings in feelings, mind in mind and dhammas in dhammas, ardent, clearly comprehending and mindful, having put away covetousness and displeasure for the world; twenty-one sections in all (MN 10). Stated fruit: final knowledge in this life or, with a residue, non-return, expected for one who develops them for seven years down to seven days (MN 10:46). Each section closes with the refrain (internal, external, both; arising, passing away; bare knowledge and recollection; independence; clinging to nothing in the world).
signs_of_progress: The text states only the fruit (mn10:46), not intermediate signs.

name: Contemplation of the body (kāyānupassanā)
method_summary: Fourteen sections: breath, postures, clear comprehension, repulsiveness of the body's parts, the four elements, and the nine charnel-ground contemplations (MN 10:4-31). Each section closes with the refrain (internal, external, both; arising, passing away; bare knowledge and recollection; independence; clinging to nothing in the world).

name: Contemplation of feelings (vedanānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing each pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as such, and as worldly (sāmisa) or unworldly (nirāmisa) (MN 10:32-33).

name: Contemplation of mind (cittānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing the mind in eight pairs: with/without lust, hatred, delusion; contracted/scattered; exalted/unexalted; surpassable/unsurpassable; concentrated/unconcentrated; liberated/unliberated (MN 10:34-35).

name: Contemplation of dhammas (dhammānupassanā)
method_summary: Five sections: the five hindrances, five aggregates of clinging, six sense bases, seven awakening factors, four noble truths (MN 10:36-45). For hindrances, fetters and awakening factors the monk knows each as present or absent and how the unarisen arises, the arisen is abandoned (or fulfilled, for the factors) and the abandoned does not arise again.

name: Contemplation of the postures (iriyāpatha)
method_summary: The monk knows 'I am walking', 'standing', 'sitting', 'lying down', and knows the body however it is disposed (MN 10:6-7).

name: Acting with clear comprehension (sampajāna)
method_summary: Acting with clear comprehension in going forward and back, looking, bending and stretching, wearing robes, eating and drinking, excreting, walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking and keeping silent (MN 10:8-9).

name: Attention to the repulsiveness of the body (paṭikūlamanasikāra)
method_summary: Reviewing the body from soles to hair-tips as bounded by skin and full of impurities, naming its parts, as a man with eyes reviews the grains in a sack (MN 10:10-11).

name: Attention to the elements (dhātumanasikāra)
method_summary: Reviewing the body, however placed, as earth, water, fire and air, like a butcher at a crossroads with the divided carcass (MN 10:12-13).

name: The nine charnel-ground contemplations (navasivathikā)
method_summary: As if seeing a discarded body in a charnel ground in nine stages (swollen, blue-black, festering; eaten by animals; skeleton with flesh and blood; without flesh, smeared with blood; without flesh and blood; scattered bones; white bones; heaped bones; rotten bones crumbled to powder), the monk compares this body with it: 'this body too is of such a nature, will become like that, and is not exempt from it' (MN 10:14-31).

name: Contemplation of the five aggregates of clinging
method_summary: Knowing form, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness, each with its arising and its passing away (MN 10:38-39).

name: Mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasati)
method_summary: In MN 10 the breath is the first section of body-contemplation: sitting in the forest, at a tree-root or in an empty hut, legs crossed, body upright, mindfulness established in front, mindfully breathing in and out; knowing long and short breaths; training in experiencing the whole body and calming the bodily formation, like a turner knowing a long or short turn (MN 10:4-5). The full sixteen steps are in MN 118.
prerequisites: Place and posture as stated in the text: forest, tree-root or empty hut; legs crossed, body upright, mindfulness established in front.
